title: Something to Chew On
style: Delta blues, gritty deep baritone in the user's own recorded voice, close and raw; 71 BPM heavy-footed shuffle with a sparse backbeat; dobro slide over fingerpicked resonator, walking bass, wailing harmonica and swelling church organ; tape saturation, mono room mic, sepia analog warmth, vintage 1960s mix.
lyrics:
[Stanza 1]
I feel unapologetic, baby, but still so wrong inside
Lord, I feel unapologetic, yet so damn wrong inside
‘Cause these desires I carry ain’t no thought crime to hide

[Stanza 2]
Old-time religion taught me sex was pure-born sin
Yeah, that old-time religion said self-joy was pure-born sin
Left me shamed for a victimless crime I kept locked in

[Stanza 3]
Now I’m progressive-leaning, preachin’ respect and consent
I’m progressive-leanin’, still provin’ I ain’t no creep, no intent
But objectifyin’ flesh is the new ideological sin they invent

[Stanza 4]
My unmet desires don’t mean nothin’ next to her aching head
These unmet desires don’t mean nothin’ next to real-world dread
Just dirty little cravings… something for the others to chew on, they said

[Stanza 5]
But that “something to chew on” cuts deeper than they know
Yeah, that petty little something still burns me down below
It’s small to the world, but it’s all the hunger I still hold
